$comment: Explained-difference rules for the legacy parity harness. A difference is 'explained' only if a rule here matches it: the artifact, a path pattern (array keys shown as *), the change (added | removed | changed), optional value constraints on the legacy and projected value, and an optional named predicate from scripts/parity/lib/predicates.mjs that checks the stated cause against the data. Everything else is 'unexplained' and fails the run. Rules are applied in order; the first match wins. A rule that matches nothing fails the run, so this file cannot rot. Keep rules narrow: a rule that would excuse a different cause than its justification names is a bug.

rules.justification: Legacy carried companion spans on must-not-flag fixtures and candidate spans on unresolved (T0) fixtures. A silent control asserts no secret, and an unresolved fixture asserts nothing, so the importer dropped those spans and counted them (docs/migration/cases-report.md: companion-span-on-must-not-flag, t0-candidate-spans). Checked: the legacy fixture is must-not-flag or T0 and the canonical outcome is must-not-flag or not-assertable.

The same dropped spans seen from the other side: the projected fixture has an empty span list where legacy had candidate or companion spans. Same predicate as spans-not-carried-on-silent-or-unresolved.

in: Locally constructed synthetic value; never issued by a provider.
Synthetic credential-shaped test value; never issued by a provider.
Deterministically constructed synthetic token; never issued by GitHub.

rules.justification: These three sentences repeat on every span and say only that the value is synthetic. That statement is recorded once per fixture set in `notes` (docs/governance/safety.md), so the importer kept a span note only when it was not one of these sentences. Checked: the dropped note is exactly one of the three.

The legacy display group label is not canonical. The canonical grouping of the same fixtures is the case, so the projection fills `group` with the case id. A legacy consumer that displays the group shows the case id. Checked: the projected value is the fixture's case id.

Legacy carries one prose reason per fixture. A canonical case records one rationale: the most common reason among its fixtures (whitespace-normalized, clipped at 2000 characters), after a note when the evidence basis was downgraded. The projection repeats the case rationale on each fixture. Checked: the projected text is the case rationale and equals a legacy reason of a fixture in the same case (or its clipped prefix).

Legacy tier T2 is tool-corroborated. The evidence-classes rule (docs/governance/evidence-classes.md) needs artifacts from two distinct owners; where the cited sources do not have them the importer recorded the case as project-policy, which projects back as T3. The downgrade is written in the case rationale (docs/migration/cases-report.md: T2 recorded as project-policy). Checked: the case basis is project-policy and its rationale carries the downgrade note.

Legacy kind must-redact exists only for tiers T1 and T2; project-policy positives are kind policy. A T2 fixture downgraded to T3 (assessment-tier-downgraded-on-import) therefore changes kind with its tier. Same predicate.

An unresolved (T0) fixture was unscored in legacy and is not-assertable here, with its candidate spans dropped, so whether it was authored as must-redact or must-not-flag is not canonical. The projection emits must-not-flag with no spans and tier T0. Legacy consumers key T0 on the tier (lattice groupKey 'pending/T0', scoring skips T0), not the kind. Checked: the legacy tier is T0 and the canonical outcome is not-assertable.

The legacy corpus loader (validateCorpus) rejects a twin whose positive has no secret span. A positive that was unresolved (T0) is not-assertable here with its candidate spans dropped, so projecting the twin link would make the corpus unloadable. The projection omits twinOf, mutation and mutationKind on such twins; the lineage stays canonical (the case relation and the fixture lineage in records/). Checked: the legacy twin target is a fixture whose canonical outcome is not-assertable.
Same as twin-fields-omitted-for-unresolved-positive, for the fixture index, whose legacy builder also requires the twin target to be a positive with a secret span.

Canonical citations are recorded per case, not per fixture, so each projected fixture lists the union of its case. Checked: the added URL is cited by another fixture of the same case in the legacy corpus.

The taxonomy import mints an evidence source only for URLs cited by the legacy taxonomy, dossiers and contracts. A fixture assessment may cite a URL that none of those cite (for example a project-owned commit or issue link); the case import could not link it and dropped it, counted as assessment-source-not-in-taxonomy-import. Checked: the legacy citation is not a URL, or its base URL is not a canonical evidence source.

The projected citation list is empty because every legacy citation of the fixture is unrecorded (assessment-sources-not-recorded). Checked: every legacy citation of the fixture fails the recorded-source test.

Which product detector is expected to fire (detectors, arrivalTargets, assessment.contract) is a scanner/product assignment. Canonical data is scanner-neutral and never records it (ADR 0005, what is dropped). A consumer supplies it through the `fixture-detectors` and `corpus-fixture-extras` overlays (overlay-interface.json).

Expected product action (warn/redact/block), policy-family bookkeeping and the policy-conformance subset flag are Redact Secret policy, not credential facts (ADR 0005, what is dropped). Supplied by the `corpus-fixture-extras` overlay.

formatReason repeats prose already carried as the assessment reason; `issue` is the product issue a fixture was written for, kept canonically only as an externalRefs pointer on the case (ADR 0005). Supplied by the `corpus-fixture-extras` overlay when a consumer needs them.

Suite-level legacy review labels (reviewStatus, scope, references, milestoneReview) describe the legacy review process and a product milestone. The construction statement and legacy review status survive as the fixture set's `notes` (ADR 0005); the milestone record is product release bookkeeping and is not imported.
supportStatus is Redact Secret qualification (stable/provisional/pending), which canonical data must never carry (ARCHITECTURE: evidence model). Supplied by the `taxonomy-support-status` overlay.

A legacy `sources` entry that is internal prose (for example 'benchmarks/lib/assessment.ts (classifyFixture variant guard...)') is not a citable source; the importer dropped it and counted it (dropped:taxonomy-source-not-a-url). Checked: the legacy entry is not an https URL.
The legacy sourceNote is hand-written history of issue #502. The projection replaces it with an explicit generated-data marker so nobody mistakes the file for hand-authored legacy data.

The dossier tier is re-expressed as the evidence class of the dossier research claim (ADR 0004). A T2 claim without artifacts from two distinct owners imports as unresolved, which projects back as T0; a dossier with no tier (null) and a researched verdict also imports as unresolved, and T0 is the projection's reading. Both are counted in docs/migration/taxonomy-report.md (downgrade:tool-corroborated-fewer-than-two-owners).

corpora/development/shadow-scoring-authored.json is a calibration-only tuning input (calibrationOnly: true), excluded from the published fixture index by legacy itself. It is not evidence and is not imported. Checked: the legacy category is marked calibrationOnly.

Canonical family and scenario links are recorded per case, so each projected fixture carries the union of its case. Checked: the added family or scenario is listed by legacy for another fixture of the same case.

A legacy fixture with no family (an unscoped global control) shares a case with fixtures that do have families, so the case-level union gives it those families and the unscoped reason no longer applies. Checked: the canonical case has at least one family.

Same cause as semantics-families-case-union, seen in the fixture index: family and scenario links are recorded per case in canonical records, so each projected fixture carries the union of its case. Checked: the added family or scenario is listed by legacy for another fixture of the same case.

Same cause as semantics-unscoped-replaced-by-case-families, seen in the fixture index: an unscoped legacy fixture shares a case with scoped ones, so the case-level union gives it families and the unscoped reason no longer applies. Checked: the canonical case has at least one family.

The product issue, release milestone and release a fixture belongs to are Redact Secret release bookkeeping. Canonical cases keep the product issue only as an externalRefs pointer at case level. Supplied by the `fixture-provenance` overlay.

These digests are SHA-256 over the reviewed metadata, the taxonomy and the index content. Those inputs differ by the explained differences listed in this report (including legacy array order), so the digests cannot match. The projected index is self-consistent: the legacy fixtureIndexProblems check, run over it in this report, finds none. Consumers that pin the legacy identity digest (peer-observations) must re-key to the projected identity.
